scenes.animation: Cricket match toss. The umpire flips a coin high; it spins in slow motion. Zippy, as captain, shouts 'Heads!' and then panics mid-air, sweating.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Heads or tails? What are my chances here?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exactly one out of two. And we can say that without tossing a single coin.

scenes.animation: Outcomes pop out of a coin as bubbles: 'H' and 'T', both the same size, labelled 'equally likely'. The formula builds: 'P(E) = Number of outcomes favourable to E / Number of all possible outcomes of the experiment'. Then 'P(H) = 1/2'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When all outcomes of an experiment are equally likely, the theoretical probability of an event E is the number of outcomes favourable to E, divided by the number of all possible outcomes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes, head and tail. So the probability of a head is one by two.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: What does equally likely really mean?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That no outcome has a better chance than another. A fair coin, a fair die, a well-shuffled deck.

scenes.animation: Worked example: a kirana-shop jar with 3 red and 5 black balls. Line by line: 'Total outcomes = 3 + 5 = 8', 'P(red) = 3/8', 'P(black) = 5/8', 'P(red) + P(black) = 3/8 + 5/8 = 8/8 = 1'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Example: a bag contains 3 red balls and 5 black balls. One ball is drawn at random.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: There are 3 plus 5, that is 8 possible outcomes. Three are red, so the probability of red is 3 by 8.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Five are black, so the probability of black is 5 by 8.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Add them: 3 by 8 plus 5 by 8 is 8 by 8, which is one.

scenes.animation: A die rolls. Card 1: 'Getting 8 on a die: 0 favourable outcomes → P = 0/6 = 0 (impossible event)'. Card 2: 'Getting a number less than 7: 6 favourable → P = 6/6 = 1 (sure event)'. A number line from 0 to 1 appears with 'Impossible' at 0 and 'Sure' at 1.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Roll a die. The chance of getting 8 is zero by six, which is zero. An event that cannot happen is an impossible event.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The chance of getting a number less than 7 is six by six, which is one. That is a sure event.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So every probability lies between 0 and 1, both included.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: if your answer is negative or bigger than one, you have made a mistake. Check it at once.

scenes.animation: Recap board with the spinning coin: '1. P(E) = favourable outcomes / total outcomes (equally likely)', '2. 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1; impossible = 0, sure = 1', '3. Probabilities of all elementary events add up to 1'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: probability is favourable outcomes divided by total outcomes, when all outcomes are equally likely.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: it always lies from 0 to 1. Impossible is 0, sure is 1.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the probabilities of all the elementary events of an experiment add up to one.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Called heads. Got tails. Still fifty-fifty, I suppose.

name: Complementary Events and Coins, Dice and Cards

scenes.animation: A Diwali card party. Zippy stares at a shuffled deck, trying to count every card that is 'not an ace', finger-counting furiously as numbers overflow above his head.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Probability of not getting an ace? I'm counting 48 cards one by one!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Stop counting. Find the chance of an ace, and subtract it from one.

scenes.animation: A circle labelled 'All outcomes' splits into two parts: 'E' in green and 'not E' (Ē) in grey, together filling the circle. The equation builds: 'P(E) + P(not E) = 1', then 'P(not E) = 1 − P(E)'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The event not E happens exactly when E does not happen. E and not E are called complementary events.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Together they cover every outcome, so P of E plus P of not E equals one.

scenes.animation: The deck fans out into four suits of 13 cards: spades and clubs in black, hearts and diamonds in red. Face cards King, Queen and Jack glow: '3 × 4 = 12 face cards'. Worked lines: 'P(ace) = 4/52 = 1/13', 'P(not ace) = 1 − 1/13 = 12/13', 'P(face card) = 12/52 = 3/13'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A deck has 52 cards in four suits of 13: spades, hearts, diamonds and clubs. Hearts and diamonds are red; spades and clubs are black.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: There are 4 aces, so the probability of an ace is 4 by 52, which is 1 by 13.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: So the probability of not an ace is 1 minus 1 by 13, which is 12 by 13.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: King, queen and jack are face cards, 12 in all. So the probability of a face card is 12 by 52, that is 3 by 13.

scenes.animation: A die rolls: faces 1 to 6. Primes 2, 3, 5 glow gold; 1, 4, 6 stay grey. Lines: 'P(prime) = 3/6 = 1/2', 'P(not prime) = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2'. Then two coins flip: 'HH, HT, TH, TT', 'P(at least one head) = 1 − P(TT) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Now a die. The primes are 2, 3 and 5, so the probability of a prime is 3 by 6, which is one half. Not prime is also one half.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Isn't 1 a prime too?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: No. One is neither prime nor composite. That's a classic trap.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two coins tossed together give four outcomes: HH, HT, TH and TT. At least one head is the complement of no head, so it is 1 minus 1 by 4, which is 3 by 4.

scenes.animation: A 'BOARD TIP' card: 'Words like "not" and "at least one" → use 1 − P(E). Face cards = J, Q, K only (ace is not a face card).'

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: whenever you see not or at least one, think complement. It saves time and mistakes.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: And remember, an ace is not a face card.

scenes.animation: Recap board with a card, a die and a coin: '1. P(E) + P(not E) = 1', '2. Deck: 52 cards, 4 suits × 13, 12 face cards', '3. Die: primes 2, 3, 5; two coins: HH, HT, TH, TT'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: complementary events add up to one, so P of not E is one minus P of E.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: a deck has 52 cards, four suits of 13, and 12 face cards.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: on a die, the primes are 2, 3 and 5; two coins give four equally likely outcomes.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Deck shuffled. Brain unshuffled.
